messages:
SamW: Heads-up — seeing a perf regression in small-batch long-sequence runs after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. p99 latency up ~18% on 1k tokens. nsys shows a big spike in cudaMemcpy on the hotpath.
Anya: Ugh. Do you have traces? which workload/commit?
SamW: Trace links: gs://perf-traces/2026-03-18/after_nsys.qdtrace and gs://perf-traces/2026-03-18/before_nsys.qdtrace. Suspect commit a1b2c3d4 (kernel-selector: prefer mem-avoid kernel when seq<128).
RajP: Can you paste the nsys command you used? I'll run a before/after compare on my workstation.
SamW: Captured with nvtx spans in runner. Command i ran:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_after --capture-range=none --trace=cuda,osrt -w true --kill=none --sample=none --duration=60 --external=1 
```
Then exported to qdrep and opened in Nsight. Key observation: there's a repeated cudaMemcpyAsync (~5-6us each) per-token around the KV load path; overall it's ~28% of GPU time vs ~2% in before trace.
perf-bot: CI bisect suggests the regression lands at commit a1b2c3d4 (author: anya), reverting that patch restores baseline on our perf smoke.
Anya: That's the kernel probe change where selector prefers small-block kernel if average seq < 128. I thought it reduced register pressure. It shouldn't introduce copies.
RajP: Could be a change in fallback for mixed-dtype buffers that forces an extra staging memcpy. Look at the runtime path: kernel_selector -> variant_prober -> staging_copy. In the trace I see NVTX span "kv_load" then a separate span "staging_memcpy" that didn't exist before.
SamW: Exact. In the after trace the timeline has:
- NVTX: run_forward
- NVTX: kv_load (kernel)
- cudaMemcpyAsync (device->device?) labeled staging_memcpy
- NVTX: kernel_exec
The memcpy aligns with the selector choosing the "packed-kernel" which expects packed KV layout, so runtime emits a copy to pack it.
Anya: Hmm. Can you grep the logs for "selector=packed-kernel" and "staging_copy"?
SamW: Done. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] selector: packed-kernel chosen (shape=(1,1024))
[2026-03-18T09:12:23Z] runtime: staging_copy required=true bytes=524288
```
And compare to before: packed-kernel was chosen less often and staging_copy=false.
RajP: So the selector change increased packed-kernel picks on long sequences for small batches which triggers pack-copy. That explains extra memcpy overhead scaling with seq length.
Anya: Two options: 1) tighten the probe so packed-kernel only chosen when input already packed (avoid copy), 2) add an in-place pack path or fuse pack into kernel, or 3) revert for now.
SamW: For quick mitigation we toggled KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE_STRICT=true in staging and reran perf: p99 back to baseline. However that's a blunt revert (makes runtime less flexible).
perf-bot: Created perf ticket PERF-1428 linking traces and bisect: https://redwood.internal/perf/1428
RajP: For next steps I'll: run a perf sweep across seq lengths 128/512/1024 with both selectors and capture nsys stacks, then open a perfetto diff to annotate the spans. Also file a small repro that triggers pack-copy to try a fused kernel locally.
Anya: I'll draft a follow-up patch that: only prefers packed-kernel when buffer.is_packed || batch_size>1 OR we can query buffer_layout_hint. If that fails we should at least avoid per-token memcopy (aggregate pack once per batch).
SamW: Agreed. Action items:
- Raj: perf sweep + nsys traces (today)
- Anya: draft selector guard and unit test (tomorrow)
- Sam: keep KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE_STRICT=true in staging until we have fix
- perf-bot: attach bisect + traces to PERF-1428
Thanks — will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
